title: Employees are vibe-coding their own apps. Cloudflare open-sources Void to give IT a handle on them
key_facts: On Thursday (15 Oct 2026) Cloudflare released Void, a collection of three open-source tools including a self-hosted platform to deploy and manage employees' AI-built apps.
The three parts are the Void SDK (building blocks for full-stack apps with Vite), the Void CLI (deployment) and Void Platform (a shared environment with an admin dashboard).
Administrators can set who can deploy and access apps, inspect deployments and logs, monitor resource use and set usage limits.
Void began at VoidZero, which Cloudflare acquired in June; Evan You (founder of VoidZero) said it no longer needs to be a commercial product, so it is open source.
Void's docs show admins can make new apps public by default and there is no mandatory IT security review before an app goes live; companies would have to build approval steps themselves.
Self-hosting needs a paid Cloudflare Workers for Platforms plan from $25 a month, R2 storage and a separately hosted PostgreSQL database; there is no managed version yet.
Cloudflare uses Void Platform internally, restricted to employees.
quote_evidence: On Thursday, the company announced the release of Void, a collection of three open-source tools that includes a self-hosted platform where companies can deploy and manage their employees’ AI-built applications.
Void’s documented deployment process also contains no mandatory IT security review before an application goes live.
why_it_matters_hint: Employees building their own apps with AI is creating unmanaged 'shadow IT'; Void gives companies a place to host and control such apps, with limits.
notes: Announcement a day before the window; reported 16 Oct.
